core_obligations: Write the polynomial with its coefficients and form the quotient of the polynomial ring by that polynomial (proof lines 4575-4577).
Take the class of the variable as the root and check that the polynomial vanishes at it (proof lines 4577-4578).
Quote the divisibility statement for monic polynomials to factor the polynomial as the product of the linear factor and a monic quotient (proof lines 4579-4580).
proof_roadmap: Construct the finite free extension (proof lines 4575-4577).
Factor using the one-root statement (proof lines 4579-4581).
difficulty_reason: The lemma adjoins a root of a monic polynomial by a finite free ring extension, and the proof is a 7-line construction that writes the extension down explicitly. It forms the quotient of a polynomial ring by the polynomial itself, so that the class of the variable is a root, observes that the quotient is finite free over the base because the polynomial is monic, and then quotes the statement that a monic polynomial over a ring is divisible by the linear factor corresponding to any of its roots to obtain the announced factorisation. The two steps — the explicit finite free extension and the appeal to the divisibility statement — are each displayed.
